Trigonometric Functions of Angles of a Triangle
solution:
[Textbook misprint: an unclosed bracket — the working prints \(= 2\sin C\left[\cos(A-B) + \cos(A+B)\right.\) with no closing bracket. Closed here as the mathematics requires; no step or value is changed.]

L.H.S. \(= \sin 2A + \sin 2B - \sin 2C\)

\(= 2\sin\left(\dfrac{2A + 2B}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{2A - 2B}{2}\right) - \sin 2C\)

\(= 2\sin(A + B)\cos(A - B) - 2\sin C\,\cos C\)

\(= 2\sin(\pi - C)\cos(A - B) - 2\sin C\,\cos\left[\pi - (A + B)\right]\)

\(= 2\sin C\,\cos(A - B) + 2\sin C\,\cos(A + B)\)

\(= 2\sin C\,[\cos(A - B) + \cos(A + B)\)

\(= 2\sin C \cdot 2\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B + A + B}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B - A - B}{2}\right)\)

\(= 4\sin C\,\cos A\,\cos B\)

\(= 4\cos A\,\cos B\,\sin C\)

\(=\) R.H.S.
_note: Printed defect, transcribed as-is: the sixth step opens a square bracket that is never closed — the book prints "= 2sinC [cos (A - B) + cos(A+ B)" with no closing "]".

subtopic: Trigonometric Functions of Angles of a Triangle
solution:
L.H.S \(= \cos A + \cos B + \cos C\)

\(= 2\cos\left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) + 1 - 2\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}\)

\(= 2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{C}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) + 1 - 2\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}\)

\(= 1 + 2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\,\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) - 2\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}\)

\(= 1 + 2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) - \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\right]\)

\(= 1 + 2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) - \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{A + B}{2}\right)\right]\)

\(= 1 + 2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) - \cos\left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right)\right]\)

\(= 1 + 2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\cdot 2\sin\left(\dfrac{A - B + A + B}{4}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{A + B - A + B}{4}\right)\)

\(= 1 + 4\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\,\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\,\sin\dfrac{B}{2}\)

\(= 1 + 4\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\,\sin\dfrac{B}{2}\,\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\)

\(=\) R.H.S.

subtopic: Trigonometric Functions of Angles of a Triangle
stem: \(\sin^2 A + \sin^2 B - \sin^2 C = 2\sin A\,\sin B\,\cos C\)
solution:
[Textbook misprint: one line prints \(= 1 - \sin^2 C - \cos(A+B) + \cos(A-B)\), with a \(+\) where a PRODUCT is required — as printed that line follows from neither the line above nor the line below, both of which need \(\cos(A+B)\cdot\cos(A-B)\). The same solution also prints a lower-case \(\sin^2 c\) mid-working.]

L.H.S. \(= \sin^2 A + \sin^2 B - \sin^2 C\)

\(= \dfrac{1 - \cos 2A}{2} + \dfrac{1 - \cos 2B}{2} - \sin^2 C\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[2 - \cos 2A - \cos 2B\right] - \sin^2 C\)

\(= 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\cos 2A + \cos 2B\right] - \sin^2 c\)

\(= 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cos\left(\dfrac{2A + 2B}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{2A - 2B}{2}\right) - \sin^2 C\)

\(= 1 - \sin^2 C - \cos(A + B) + \cos(A - B)\)

\(= \cos^2 C - \cos\left[\pi - C\right]\cos(A - B)\)

\(= \cos^2 C + \cos C\,\cos(A - B)\)

\(= \cos C\left[\cos C + \cos(A - B)\right]\)

\(= \cos C\left[\cos\left[\pi - (A + B)\right] + \cos(A - B)\right]\)

\(= \cos C\left[-\cos(A + B) + \cos(A - B)\right]\)

\(= \cos C\left[\cos(A - B) - \cos(A + B)\right]\)

\(= \cos C \cdot 2\sin\left(\dfrac{A - B + A + B}{2}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{A + B - A + B}{2}\right)\)

\(= 2\cos C\,\sin A\,\sin B\)

\(= 2\sin A\,\sin B\,\cos C\)

\(=\) R. H.S.
_note: Two printed defects, transcribed as-is. (1) The fourth step prints a lower-case "c" — "- sin^2 c" — where every other line of the same solution uses capital C. (2) The sixth step prints a "+" between the two cosines, "= 1 - sin^2 C - cos(A + B) + cos (A- B)", where the preceding line and the following line both require the PRODUCT cos(A + B) cos(A - B); as printed the line does not follow from the one above it and the next line does not follow from it.

subtopic: Trigonometric Functions of Angles of a Triangle
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the STATEMENT is printed \(\cot A\cot B + \cot B\cot{} + \cot C\cot A = 1\) — the second product's second factor is missing. The book's own closing line of this same solution prints the intended \(\cot A\cot B + \cot B\cot C + \cot C\cot A = 1\).]

In \(\Delta ABC\), \(A + B + C = \pi\)

\(\therefore A + B = \pi - C\)

\(\therefore \tan(A + B) = \tan(\pi - C)\)

\(\therefore \dfrac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A\,\tan B} = \tan(\pi - C)\)

\(\therefore \tan A + \tan B = -\tan C + \tan A\,\tan B\,\tan C\)

\(\therefore \tan A + \tan B + \tan C = \tan A\,\tan B\,\tan C\)

\(\therefore \dfrac{1}{\cot A} + \dfrac{1}{\cot B} + \dfrac{1}{\cot C} = \dfrac{1}{\cot A}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\cot B}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\cot C}\)

\(\therefore \cot A\,\cot B + \cot B\,\cot C + \cot C\,\cot A = 1\)
_note: Printed defect in the STATEMENT, transcribed as-is: the book prints "cotA cot B + cot B cot + cot C  cotA = 1" — the second product's second factor is missing, i.e. "cot B cot" has no angle after it. The intended statement is cotA cotB + cotB cotC + cotC cotA = 1, which is exactly what the book's own final line of this solution prints.

subtopic: Trigonometric Functions of Angles of a Triangle
solution:
In \(\Delta ABC\), \(A + B + C = \pi\)

\(\therefore A + B = \pi - C\)  \(\therefore \dfrac{A + B}{2} = \dfrac{\pi - C}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{C}{2}\)

\(\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2} + \dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{C}{2}\right)\)

\(\therefore \dfrac{\tan\dfrac{A}{2} + \tan\dfrac{B}{2}}{1 - \tan\dfrac{A}{2}\,\tan\dfrac{B}{2}} = \cot\dfrac{C}{2}\)

\(\therefore \dfrac{\tan\dfrac{A}{2} + \tan\dfrac{B}{2}}{1 - \tan\dfrac{A}{2}\,\tan\dfrac{B}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\tan\dfrac{C}{2}}\)

\(\therefore \left[\tan\dfrac{A}{2} + \tan\dfrac{B}{2}\right]\tan\dfrac{C}{2} = 1 - \tan\dfrac{A}{2}\,\tan\dfrac{B}{2}\)

\(\therefore \tan\dfrac{A}{2}\,\tan\dfrac{C}{2} + \tan\dfrac{B}{2}\,\tan\dfrac{C}{2} = 1 - \tan\dfrac{A}{2}\,\tan\dfrac{B}{2}\)

\(\therefore \tan\dfrac{A}{2}\,\tan\dfrac{C}{2} + \tan\dfrac{B}{2}\,\tan\dfrac{C}{2} + \tan\dfrac{A}{2}\,\tan\dfrac{B}{2} = 1\)

subtopic: Trigonometric Functions of Angles of a Triangle
stem: \(\dfrac{\cos A - \cos B + \cos C + 1}{\cos A + \cos B + \cos C - 1} = \cot\dfrac{A}{2}\,\cot\dfrac{C}{2}\)
solution:
L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\cos A - \cos B + \cos C + 1}{\cos A + \cos B + \cos C - 1}\)

\(= \dfrac{\left[\cos A - \cos B\right] + \left[1 + \cos C\right]}{\left[\cos A + \cos B\right] - \left[1 - \cos C\right]}\)

\(= \dfrac{2\sin\left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right) + 2\cos^2\dfrac{C}{2}}{2\cos\left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) + \left(-2\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}\right)}\)

\(= \dfrac{2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{c}{2}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right) + 2\cos^2\dfrac{C}{2}}{2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{c}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) + \left(-2\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}\right)}\)

\(= \dfrac{2\cos\dfrac{C}{2}\,\sin\left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right) + 2\cos^2\dfrac{C}{2}}{2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\,\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) - 2\sin^2\dfrac{C}{2}}\)

\(= \dfrac{\cos\dfrac{C}{2}\left[\sin\left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right) + \cos\dfrac{C}{2}\right]}{\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) - \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\right]}\)

\(= \cot\dfrac{C}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\left[\sin\left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right) + \sin\left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right)\right]}{\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) - \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{A + B}{2}\right)\right]}\)

\(= \cot\dfrac{C}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right) + \sin\left(\dfrac{B - A}{2}\right)}{\cos\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) - \cos\left(\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right)}\)

\(= \cot\dfrac{C}{2}\cdot\dfrac{2\sin\dfrac{\dfrac{A + B}{2} + \dfrac{B - A}{2}}{2}\,\cos\dfrac{\dfrac{A + B}{2} - \dfrac{B - A}{2}}{2}}{2\sin\dfrac{\dfrac{A - B}{2} + \dfrac{A + B}{2}}{2}\,\sin\dfrac{\dfrac{A + B}{2} - \dfrac{A - B}{2}}{2}}\)

\(= \cot\dfrac{C}{2}\cdot\dfrac{2\sin\dfrac{B}{2}\,\cos\dfrac{A}{2}}{2\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\,\sin\dfrac{B}{2}}\)

\(= \cot\dfrac{C}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\cos\dfrac{A}{2}}{\sin\dfrac{A}{2}}\)

\(= \cot\dfrac{C}{2}\,\cot\dfrac{A}{2}\)

\(=\) R.H.S.
_note: Printed defect, transcribed as-is: the fourth step of the solution prints a lower-case "c" in both \(\sin(\pi/2 - c/2)\) and \(\cos(\pi/2 - c/2)\), where the angle is the capital C of the triangle (every neighbouring line uses capital C).
